policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word order only (τῶν ὧδε / ὧδε τῶν); ASV 'some here of them that stand by' renders either arrangement.
Presence or absence of the article before Ἰωάννην leaves no trace in ASV 'and John'.
Singular/plural verb with the neuter plural subject τὰ ἱμάτια; ASV 'his garments became' is the same English either way.
ASV reads only 'exceeding white' and has no rendering of ὡς χιών ('as snow'), which RP adds.
ASV 'so as no fuller on earth can whiten them' renders ὡς with or without the correlative οὕτως.
Word order only; ASV 'three tabernacles' renders either arrangement.
ASV 'he knew not what to answer' renders ἀποκριθῇ; RP λαλήσει would give 'what to say/speak'.
ASV 'they became sore afraid' renders ἐγένοντο; RP ἦσαν would give 'they were sore afraid'.
ASV 'there came a cloud' fits ἐγένετο as readily as ἦλθεν.
Word order only; ASV 'hear ye him' renders either arrangement.
Both readings say the same thing ('save Jesus only with themselves'); the ἀλλά/εἰ μή and order difference is not distinguished in the English.
ASV's opening 'And' renders καί or postpositive δέ indifferently.
ἐκ and ἀπὸ νεκρῶν are both 'from the dead'.
Word order only; ASV 'tell no man what things they had seen' renders either arrangement.
ASV 'And he said unto them' renders bare ἔφη; RP ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν would give 'answering said'.
Alternate present forms of ἀποκαθίστημι; ASV 'restoreth' renders either.
Orthographic variation in ἐξουδεν(η/ω)θῇ; ASV 'be set at nought' renders either.
Imperfect/aorist of θέλω; ASV 'whatsoever they would' renders either.
ASV 'when they came to the disciples, they saw' has plural verbs, matching ἐλθόντες … εἶδον; RP's singular would give 'when he came … he saw'.
πρὸς αὐτούς and the plain dative αὐτοῖς are both 'with them'.
εὐθύς/εὐθέως are alternate forms; ASV 'straightway' renders either.
ASV construes the collective 'multitude' with plural verbs regardless, so plural and singular Greek yield the same English.
ASV 'he asked them' renders the pronoun αὐτούς; RP τοὺς γραμματεῖς would give 'he asked the scribes'.
ASV 'What question ye with them?' renders non-reflexive αὐτούς; the reflexive αὑτούς would give 'among yourselves'.
ASV 'one of the multitude answered him' has a single finite verb with the dative, excluding RP's ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν; the base and r01 are the same wording and are not distinguished.
ἐάν/ἄν in the indefinite clause; ASV 'wheresoever' renders either.
English requires the possessive in 'grindeth his teeth' whether or not αὐτοῦ stands in the Greek.
ASV 'he answereth them' renders plural αὐτοῖς; RP αὐτῷ would give 'him'.
Word order and εὐθύς/εὐθέως only; ASV 'straightway the spirit' renders either.
ASV 'tare him grievously' renders the intensive compound συνεσπάραξεν; simple ἐσπάραξεν is 'tare him' (cf. ASV 1:26 'tearing him').
παιδιόθεν alone already means 'from a child'; ASV 'From a child' does not require the preposition ἐκ.
Word order and the article on πῦρ leave no trace: ASV renders 'both into the fire and into the waters' in any case.
Alternate second-person forms of δύναμαι; ASV 'if thou canst' renders either.
ASV 'If thou canst!' has no rendering of RP's added πιστεῦσαι ('if thou canst believe').
ASV begins the sentence 'Straightway the father …' with no conjunction, matching bare εὐθύς rather than καὶ εὐθύς/εὐθέως.
ASV text lacks 'with tears' and its mapped textual_variant note reports it only as an addition of many ancient authorities.
ASV reads 'I believe' with no vocative; RP adds κύριε ('Lord').
Word order and article only; ASV 'Thou dumb and deaf spirit' renders either arrangement.
Word order only; ASV 'I command thee' renders either arrangement.
Participle gender is invisible in English, and 'torn him much' supplies the object whether or not αὐτόν stands in the Greek.
ASV 'the more part said' renders the articular τοὺς πολλούς; anarthrous πολλούς would give 'many said'.
Word order and the placement of αὐτόν leave 'took him by the hand' unchanged.
Genitive absolute versus accusative-participle construction; ASV 'when he was come into the house' renders either.
Word order only; ASV 'asked him privately' renders either arrangement.
ASV reads 'save by prayer' and its mapped textual_variant note gives 'with fasting' only as an addition of many ancient authorities.
ASV 'passed through Galilee' renders the compound παρεπορεύοντο; simple ἐπορεύοντο would be 'went through'.
ASV 'after three days he shall rise again' renders μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας; RP τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ would give 'on the third day'.
ASV 'And they came to Capernaum' renders plural ἦλθον; RP ἦλθεν would give 'he came'.
ASV 'What were ye reasoning on the way?' has no rendering of RP's added πρὸς ἑαυτούς ('among yourselves').
ἄν/ἐάν in the indefinite relative clause; ASV 'Whosoever' renders either.
ἄν/ἐάν in the indefinite relative clause; ASV 'whosoever' renders either.
Present/aorist subjunctive of δέχομαι; ASV 'receiveth' renders either.
ASV 'John said unto him' renders a single ἔφη: no 'answered' for RP's ἀπεκρίθη and no 'saying' for the added λέγων.
The dative with or without ἐν is alike 'in thy name'.

ASV has the clause once — 'and we forbade him, because he followed not us' — excluding the doubled 'who followeth not us' of Treg/RP and Greeven's truncation; the base and r01 are the same wording and are not distinguished.
ASV 'not against us is for us' is first person, excluding RP's ὑμῶν; the base and r01 are the same wording and are not distinguished.
ASV renders 'because ye are Christ's' and glosses the Greek as 'in name that ye are', with no possessive for RP's added μου ('in my name').
The ASV gloss 'Greek in name that ye are' renders ὅτι with 'that', which RP omits.
Aorist subjunctive versus future indicative after οὐ μή; ASV 'shall in no wise lose' renders either.
ἄν/ἐάν in the indefinite relative clause; ASV 'whosoever' renders either.
ASV 'one of these little ones' renders τούτων, which RP omits.
ASV text reads 'that believe on me' and its mapped textual_variant note reports the omission of 'on me' only as the reading of many ancient authorities.
The ASV gloss 'Greek a millstone turned by an ass' renders μύλος ὀνικός; RP λίθος μυλικός is 'a millstone' with no ass.
Present/aorist subjunctive of σκανδαλίζω; ASV 'cause thee to stumble' renders either.
Word order and σε/σοι; ASV 'it is good for thee' renders either.
Word order only; ASV 'to enter into life' renders either arrangement.
ASV prints no verse 44, and its note at 9:45 says verses 44 and 46 are omitted by the best ancient authorities.
σε/σοι with καλόν ἐστιν; ASV 'it is good for thee' renders either.
ASV ends the verse at 'to be cast into hell', with no 'into the unquenchable fire' and no verse 46, which its note says the best ancient authorities omit.
σέ/σοι with καλόν ἐστιν; ASV 'it is good for thee' renders either.
Presence of the article with γέενναν leaves no trace in ASV 'into hell'.
ASV reads 'to be cast into hell' with no rendering of RP's added τοῦ πυρός ('of fire').
ASV reads only 'For every one shall be salted with fire' and its mapped textual_variant note gives the sacrifice clause as an addition of many ancient authorities.
Alternate forms ἅλα/ἅλας; ASV 'Salt is good' renders either.
